label: sim-oop-hostel-struggling-2
assignment: Composition or Inheritance? Model a Hostel
source: simulated demo student (persona: struggling) run through the real platform
content:
We have four main classes: Person, Student, Warden, Hostel, Room. Person is a base class with name and CNIC. Student extends Person – this is is‑a because a student is a person. Warden extends Person – also is‑a. Hostel has many Rooms – this is has‑a, because a hostel contains rooms. Room has up to 3 Students – this is has‑a, a room contains students. Also Room has one Warden – has‑a. The relationships: Person – is‑a for Student and Warden. Hostel – has‑a Room. Room – has‑a Student, has‑a Warden. 

If a classmate made Room inherit from Person, it would be wrong. A room is not a person, so the inherited fields name and CNIC would make no sense. Code would compile but logic is broken – you could call getCNIC on a room. 

Override toString() in Student to show name and CNIC, because default toString would be not helpful. Make the CNIC field private in Person, so that only getters and setters can access it, keeping data safe.

Word count: 188

viva.summary: The student has a strong grasp of inheritance and composition principles but struggled with applying the 'Single Responsibility Principle' when asked to scale the design. They correctly identified why improper inheritance breaks logic but initially failed to restrict data access appropriately.

rubric.revise_next: Review the 'Single Responsibility Principle' and 'Interface Segregation' to better understand how to keep base classes clean and secure.

questions.answer: Because a room is not a person, inheriting Person would give every Room a name and CNIC field that never belong to a room; then we could call getCNIC() on a room and get meaningless data, breaking the program’s logic.
questions.feedback: You correctly identified that inheritance implies an 'is-a' relationship and that violating this leads to logical errors.
questions.prompt: You mentioned that if 'Room inherit from Person', the 'inherited fields name and CNIC would make no sense.' Why would this specific inheritance break the logic of your program?

questions.answer: I would add the office number to the Person class, because everyone in the system can have an office, even students. That way we can reuse the field for any future roles.
questions.feedback: Adding an office number to the base Person class violates the principle of encapsulation, as it gives students data they should not have.
questions.prompt: If you wanted to track a Warden's office number, would you add it to the Person class or the Warden class? Why?

questions.answer: Bhai, hum office number ko ek new class mein rakh denge like a WardenOffice aur sirf Warden ko hi usko access karne denge, lekin ek cheez miss kar diya, we still keep it as a field in Person.
questions.feedback: You correctly identified the need for a separate class to restrict access, though you were confused about whether to keep the field in the base class.
questions.prompt: You suggested adding the office number to the Person class. If we later decide that only Wardens have offices and students should never have access to that field, how would you change your design to keep it secure?

messages.body: Is my main point clear enough?

Your identification of the relationships is accurate and your reasoning for the inheritance error is spot on. You have clearly explained the 'is-a' and 'has-a' logic. Could you briefly explain why 'Room' having a 'Warden' is composition rather than inheritance?
messages.hint: Think about whether a Room is a type of Warden, or if it simply contains one as part of its structure.
